meetings.headline: Town Meeting rejected new authority to amend the capital plan, but approved Marshall Park engineering funding.
meetings.summary: This special town meeting acted on 15 warrant articles: it approved FY23 budget adjustments, a police union contract's first-year funding, $184,000 for Marshall Park engineering (to support up to $2 million in outside grants), a firefighter/reserve-officer retirement buyback provision, and a motel zoning change and a citizen-petitioned rezoning. It rejected giving town meeting authority to amend individual capital plan line items, rejected overriding the APDC's denial of Ritter Library window replacement, rejected changes to the APDC's own review bylaw, and rejected moving the annual town meeting and election from May to April.

minutes.headline: Town Meeting rejected new authority to amend the capital plan, but approved Marshall Park engineering funding.
minutes.summary: This special town meeting acted on 15 warrant articles: it approved FY23 budget adjustments, a police union contract's first-year funding, $184,000 for Marshall Park engineering (to support up to $2 million in outside grants), a firefighter/reserve-officer retirement buyback provision, and a motel zoning change and a citizen-petitioned rezoning. It rejected giving town meeting authority to amend individual capital plan line items, rejected overriding the APDC's denial of Ritter Library window replacement, rejected changes to the APDC's own review bylaw, and rejected moving the annual town meeting and election from May to April.

what_happened.line: Town Meeting rejected giving itself authority to amend individual line items in the capital plan.
It approved a transfer for final engineering and design at Marshall Park, meant to support outside grant applications.
It approved FY23 budget adjustments to town management, assessors, planning board and facilities and grounds lines.
It approved year-one funding for the new police officers' collective bargaining agreement.
It rejected overriding the APDC's denial of Ritter Library window replacement and rejected changing the APDC's own review bylaw.

why_it_matters: The capital plan vote leaves individual project funding outside town meeting's amending power unless a future warrant article changes the bylaw again.
Marshall Park funding lets the town move ahead on grant applications that the project depends on to cover a large share of its cost.
The Ritter Library and APDC bylaw votes leave the historic commission's review process and the library's window question unresolved.

meetings.headline: Town Meeting passed the FY23 town/school budget and capital plan, and cut back old primary school park funding by floor amendment.
meetings.summary: This was Lunenburg's annual Town Meeting, working through a full warrant covering the FY23 town and school operating budget, the capital plan, a new facilities director position, and numerous bylaw and building articles including the Woodruff property cleanup, old primary school demolition, sewer bylaw waivers, a marijuana licensing fix, and the water supply protection district. Nearly every article passed, though residents amended the old primary school demolition article down from its original funding level after a lengthy, twice-redone floor debate, and repeatedly pushed back on whether the capital plan should have allowed item-by-item votes. The meeting also passed over a citizen petition to expand the sewer service area and took up a resolution supporting a new state flag, with the final tallies on the water-district and flag articles not clearly captured.

minutes.headline: Town Meeting passed the FY23 town/school budget and capital plan, and cut back old primary school park funding by floor amendment.
minutes.summary: This was Lunenburg's annual Town Meeting, working through a full warrant covering the FY23 town and school operating budget, the capital plan, a new facilities director position, and numerous bylaw and building articles including the Woodruff property cleanup, old primary school demolition, sewer bylaw waivers, a marijuana licensing fix, and the water supply protection district. Nearly every article passed, though residents amended the old primary school demolition article down from its original funding level after a lengthy, twice-redone floor debate, and repeatedly pushed back on whether the capital plan should have allowed item-by-item votes. The meeting also passed over a citizen petition to expand the sewer service area and took up a resolution supporting a new state flag, with the final tallies on the water-district and flag articles not clearly captured.

what_happened.line: Town Meeting passed the FY23 town and school operating budget as one omnibus article, funded without drawing on free cash or stabilization.
The FY23 capital plan passed as a single up-or-down total after the moderator ruled, on town counsel's advice, that individual projects could not be voted or amended separately.
After a floor debate redone once for a procedural flaw, voters cut back the old primary school article to cover demolition and design only, not the fuller park funding first proposed.
A new facilities director position was created, and free cash was approved to clean up illegally dumped waste on the town-owned Woodruff property.
Votes on the water supply protection district bylaw and a resolution on the state flag were not clearly captured on the recording.

why_it_matters: The operating budget vote sets what residents' tax bill funds for town and school services in FY23, including new police, fire and school staff positions described by the town manager and superintendent.

Because the capital plan can only be voted as one total, residents cannot currently approve or reject individual projects like the senior center HVAC or the primary school classroom AC separately — a process several people at the meeting pushed back on.
The old primary school site now has money for demolition and design, but not for a built-out park, so what that land becomes is still an open question for a future town meeting or town decision.
watch_next: Whether the primary school AC project comes back to a future town meeting as a capital request if it exceeds what the school's operating budget can absorb.
A future decision on the final design or use — park versus open space — of the old primary school lot.
